what: hotkernel new --derive: the int4_gemv target scaffolded with the new flags instead of hand-written, run once on the reference card next to the committed examples/int4_gemv_baseline.py
command: hotkernel new int4_gemv --from int4_gemv_paths:int4pack_mm --reference int4_gemv_paths:reference_fp32 --derive int4_gemv_paths:derive --inputs x,w_q,scales,zeros,w_packed,scales_and_zeros --shape 8192 --extra w:8192x8192 --rotate w --dtype bf16 --flops 134217728 --min-bytes 35684352 --out <scratch dir>
setup: run from a scratch directory holding a copy of examples/int4_gemv_paths.py (module form of the bindings); the generated _hotkernel_contract.py is byte-identical to examples/_hotkernel_contract.py; interpreter torch 2.11.0+cu128 under WSL2

generated_baseline.timing: per-call CUDA events, steady-state rotation over K buffer pairs > 2x L2, no flush

generated_candidate_blank.timing: per-call CUDA events, steady-state rotation over K buffer pairs > 2x L2, no flush

hand_written_baseline.timing: per-call CUDA events, steady-state rotation over K buffer pairs > 2x L2, no flush

labels_only.reference: the generated file says 'on the derived inputs', the hand-written one spells out the fp32 math
labels_only.derive: the generated file binds int4_gemv_paths:derive, which is make_derive(4); the hand-written one builds make_derive(INNER_K_TILES) from BASELINE_PATH
labels_only.impl: module:function versus the kernel's own name

equivalence.ms: single protocol-3 samples of a ~30 us kernel (0.0288 vs 0.0317); the per-call spread at n=1 is 10-30%, see results/int4_gemv/log.md
equivalence.why_the_hand_written_file_stays: BASELINE_PATH selects the kernel and the matching inner_k_tiles layout together, and its docstring explains what each derived input holds; the scaffold fixes one layout. Both define the same Target.
